transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith, I'm Keith. I’ve developed this intense, irrational fear of going into the ocean, even though I grew up surfing. It has gotten to the point where it's really starting to control my life, so I decided it was time to get some help.

When you think about entering the ocean, is your fear specifically focused on the possibility of being attacked by a marine animal like a shark, or is it more about the water itself, such as the fear of drowning or the depth?

It’s not about sharks or marine animals at all. It’s entirely about the water itself—specifically, the terrifying feeling of being dragged under by a rip current, losing control, and drowning. It just brings back that exact feeling of complete helplessness from when I got caught in a rip eleven months ago.
Since that incident eleven months ago, do you find yourself having unwanted, intrusive memories or nightmares about being caught in that rip current?

No, I don't really get nightmares or random flashbacks out of the blue. It’s more that those thoughts and that panic are only triggered when I'm actually near the ocean or trying to picture myself going back into the water.
